subject: POC traffic acceptance and burst profile — next steps & ownership
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novatek.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:07:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & immediate asks — Novatek POC traffic

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can convert the verbal agreement into a concrete POC plan.

Summary (from our side)
- Goal: 2-week POC to validate NovaSearch query assistants at scale; target production-like traffic and latency profile.
- Success criteria (initial): 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for 512-token requests under baseline concurrency; no more than 2% token-level regression vs current baseline on quality evals.
- Scope: read-only query generation (no private data writes), model family: rdlw-13B-quant variant for baseline; fallback to rdlw-7B in degrade scenarios.

Traffic asks we need from you to size the trial:
1) Baseline RPS (sustained) and expected peak burst RPS, by route (search, suggestion, follow-up).
2) Typical token length distribution (median, 95th) per route — sample logs or CSV is ideal.
3) Expected concurrency (clients open sockets / sessions) and typical session burst patterns (e.g., 30s windows with spikes).
4) Any hard SLOs (latency/availability) that would block acceptance.

Action items / owners (proposed):
- Samira: share traffic matrix CSV + example payloads (attaching template) — target by EOD Thu 5/20.
- Tessa (ops): map traffic to RPS/concurrency buckets and propose the test harness — deliver Tue 5/25.
- Ben: create mutual action plan & timeline (Doc link) and coordinate access/provisioning.

Attachments: a blank traffic matrix CSV (novatek_traffic_matrix_v1.csv) and a draft success-criteria doc.

If that looks right, we can lock dates on the mutual action plan and provision a Dedicated slot for your POC.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novatek.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 17:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — Novatek POC traffic

Ben / Tessa — thanks for the clear writeup. Confirming we want to proceed with the 2-week POC. Quick answers inline: 

1) Baseline / peak RPS: baseline ~120 RPS across Search + Suggestion; expected peak bursts up to ~950 RPS for ~45–90s during marketing-driven spikes. Will break down by route in CSV.
2) Token lengths: median output tokens ~90; 95th ~420 for Search; Suggestion median ~28, 95th ~100. Input prompts average 30 tokens.
3) Concurrency: we see ~160 concurrent sockets sustained during business hours, spikes to ~720 concurrent during bursts.
4) Hard SLOs: client-facing SLO is p95 latency < 400ms for Search (generation only). If P95 slips >100ms for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows, we need autoscaling/fallback behavior.

I'll drop the traffic matrix and a small sample of payloads into the Drive link tonight. One note: we prefer no model state sharing outside our VPC — for the POC can you confirm Dedicated slot/network isolation options and whether logs are retained in our tenancy?

Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering | Novatek Systems
samira.khan@novatek.com

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — Novatek POC traffic (ops intake)

Thanks Samira for the quick responses — and thanks Ben for the recap. Dev / Ben — summarizing what we need from an ops/test-harness perspective and owners.

What we need to validate the POC
- Capacity mapping: convert Novatek's CSV into RPS buckets, token-length percentiles, and concurrency windows. Deliverable: a heatmap (RPS x token length) and a proposed schedule for sustained vs burst windows. Owner: Dev Patel — due 2027-05-25 EOD.
- Test harness: synthetic generator that replays session patterns (open socket concurrency + burst windows) and can sweep model variants (rdlw-13B-quant and rdlw-7B). Owner: Dev Patel + Ben — due 2027-05-28.
- Telemetry/SLIs: wire token-level latency traces, prefix cache hit rates, and fallback events to a telemetry dashboard. Owner: Tessa — dashboard by 2027-05-27.
- Isolation & retention: Samira's request: Dedicated slot + customer log retention in their tenancy. Ops: confirm technical feasibility and any additional provisioning lead time. Owner: Ben — confirm vendor/VPC options and retention policy by 2027-05-21.

Acceptance gates (proposed seed list)
1) Stability: no >1% request error rate during medium load (baseline).
2) Latency: p95 gen latency <= 400ms for Search during baseline; for bursts, graceful degradation to fallback model with latency <700ms.
3) Cost/throughput: throughput matches traffic matrix sustained RPS for 2 hours without queueing beyond threshold X (TBD after heatmap).
4) Regression: quality A/B check against sample eval set — no >3% drop in preferred metric.

Attachments: I attached a template "MVP_success_criteria.docx" and the CSV Ben sent.

Ben — please add the HubSpot deal link to the mutual action plan and loop Legal for a brief POC addendum re: isolation/retention.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Ops | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novatek.com>

Thanks Tessa — that aligns with our expectations. Confirming the schedule:
- CSV + payloads uploaded to the Drive link (see related_links) — file names start with novatek_traffic_matrix_v1.csv.
- We accept the acceptance gates listed; one addition: include an operational rollback trigger (auto-fail to rdlw-7B) when p95 latency > 600ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Dedicated slot + isolated log retention is required; Ben, please confirm available regions (we prefer us-west) and any lead time for isolated provisioning.

Once Ben confirms Dedicated availability I'll sign the mutual action plan and we can target the POC run wk of 6/7.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering | Novatek Systems
